prompt:
Paint the COMPLETE top-down map of one outdoor marsh area of a fantasy JRPG world as ONE finished game map image, in rich premium modern hi-bit pixel art (hand-placed crisp square pixels, hue-shifted colour ramps, dark warm outlines, lush natural detail), classic top-down RPG map view seen from above with a slight 3/4 tilt (tree crowns, rocks and buildings seen from above with their south-facing sides visible; NOT an isometric view, NOT a diorama, no depth-of-field, no tilt-shift, no 3D render, no perspective).

THE PLACE: A HIDDEN LOTUS POOL in the marsh: a round pool of calm teal water densely covered with big round lotus leaves and closed pale lotus buds, a plank jetty running out from the south shore to a little platform in the middle, a fringe of reeds; around it low peat hummocks with soft green grass, sedge, many tiny white and violet marsh flowers, clusters of pale mushrooms, a few clumps of weeping willows and two small black pools; a trodden footpath looping round the pool from the west to the north. Palette: teal water, fresh green leaves, olive peat, soft pale flowers. Secret, gentle, dreamlike.

The FIRST attached image is an exact LAYOUT GUIDE drawn on a 44 x 36 tile grid (each tile = 48 x 48 px of the output; the output is 2112 x 1728 px). Trace over it: your painting is laid pixel-for-pixel on top of it and used directly as the walkable game map, so every road, shore, cliff, tree mass, water body and landmark must sit exactly where it is in the guide at the same size (keep every edge within a few pixels of the guide; do not shift, shrink, mirror or re-arrange anything; keep the exact width of the roads and of the one- and two-tile gaps).

The SECOND attached image is only a STYLE REFERENCE from the same game: match its pixel-art rendering (pixel size, clusters, outlines, colour ramps, level of detail). Do NOT copy anything from it (no houses, towers, ponds, paths or objects from it).

The guide is soft colour-coding only (its blurred edges only mean the edge is natural and free-flowing): do NOT copy its flat colours, straight tile steps, circles or stripes. Interpret every area as the real material with rich natural variation, and give shores, woods, meadows and cliffs natural, organic, slightly irregular outlines (bulging or receding by at most a third of a tile around the guide edge). Make it feel like a real, exciting place to explore, full of small natural detail.

Guide colour key:
- olive green = PEAT MEADOW (walkable): soft damp olive-green grass on peat, small tufts, puddles, footprints.
- olive with short strokes = SEDGE TUSSOCKS (walkable, low).
- green with little dots = MARSH FLOWERS in the grass (walkable, low).
- mid brown band = the MUDDY ROAD: trodden wet earth with ruts, puddles and a few flat stones (walkable).
- darker brown = a narrow FOOTPATH of trodden earth (walkable).
- grey-brown patch = bare wet MUD FLAT (walkable).
- brown boards = a BOARDWALK / plank bridge on posts (walkable deck).
- light grey with block lines = old worn FLAGSTONES (walkable, flat).
- teal = OPEN LAKE / POOL WATER (not walkable): calm grey-teal water with lily pads and ripples.
- black-teal = a BLACK BOG POOL (not walkable): dark still water, a little duckweed.
- golden with vertical strokes = a dense bed of TALL REEDS / bulrushes (not walkable).
- round green crowns = WILLOWS / gnarled swamp trees (not walkable).
- very dark green masses = DROWNED DEAD WOOD: dense dark twisted dead trees standing in black water (not walkable).
- grey circles = BOULDERS or old tree STUMPS (not walkable).
- grey with horizontal strata = a grey ROCK RIDGE (not walkable): weathered grey rock with heather, sheer faces facing south.
Landmarks (paint each exactly on its block, at the block's size):

Walkable areas must stay walkable-looking: no boulders, trees, fences or objects standing on them unless the guide shows them.

Pixel art rules: crisp square pixels, no blur, no anti-aliasing, no painterly brush strokes, no noise, clear clusters, hue-shifted ramps. Characters in this game are about 72 output px tall, so details should be at that scale.
Lighting: this is the ALBEDO base layer (the game darkens it into night at runtime and adds lamp light on top). Neutral, soft, even daylight-like light as in the style reference; NO darkness, NO night tint, NO long cast shadows, NO light pools, NO glow, NO vignette, NO mist, NO fog, NO clouds over the map.
Do NOT paint any characters, people, animals, monsters, birds, treasure chests, lanterns, lamp posts, torches, campfires, tents, signs, signposts, text, letters, numbers, labels, grid lines, borders, frames or UI. Those are added later as separate sprites: leave the ground open for them.
revised_prompt: Create ONE complete finished 2112×1728 top-down walkable JRPG marsh map by IMAGE-TO-IMAGE PAINTOVER of the FIRST supplied image. FIRST image is the absolutely binding, pixel-registered spatial layout: retain EXACT positions, footprints, size, width and connectivity of central irregular teal pool, south-to-center vertical wooden jetty and broad little platform, left and right roads and south road, all dark bog pools (including western edge, upper-left long thin pool, southwest big pool and southeast little pool), tree clusters and isolated trees, individual reeds and grassy/meadow masses, footpaths, mud patches. DO NOT move, enlarge, shrink, mirror, simplify, or cover existing features. Stay within ~a few pixels of guide boundaries; naturalize outlines only very locally. SECOND image is purely rendering reference: match premium rich fine-cluster CRISP hand-placed square pixel art, restrained dark warm contours, hue-shifted ramps, worn wooden planks, organic peat grass, refined surface detail, NOT its objects/layout. View straight top down with slightly visible south faces of tree crowns/wood edges (NOT isometric/perspective). Depict a hidden dreamy lotus marsh in neutral EVEN daylight albedo: central water calm soft grey-teal with MANY large round light fresh-green lotus leaves, delicate closed pale white/pink lotus buds, subtle pixelated ripples, leaf grouping avoiding obstruction of wooden central platform; waterline a fringe of sedges and scattered golden bulrushes ONLY on indicated fringes; olive peat walkable meadows with compact sedge tufts, many small delicate white/violet marsh flowers in guide flower areas, pale mushrooms, footprints, small puddles, moss; gnarled drooping willow canopy clusters only over guide tree crowns. Make path and muddy road visibly clear, flat, entirely unobstructed; keep illustrated exact narrow gaps and passage widths. Render two isolated black pools plus other dark-water guide patches in existing locations, duckweed. Raised deck wood detail, lightly weathered, correct platform silhouette and vertical boardwalk. No graphic guide colors, simple circle crowns or guide-marker dots; translate all into organic richly realized pixel sprites aligned to their guide positions. No characters/creatures, no structures beyond indicated boardwalk, no labels, icons, text, lettering, UI, signs or frames; NO lighting FX, shadow pools, fog, glow, vignette, blur, smooth brushwork, noise or antialiasing. Entire canvas is the seamless final gameplay map; do not draw tiles/grid.
